examples.ko: 가을에는 단감이 맛있어서 매일 하나씩 먹어요.
examples.en: Sweet persimmons are delicious in fall, so I eat one every day.
I bought a box of sweet persimmons at the market.

examples.ko: 단감은 홍시와 달리 딱딱할 때 먹어도 달아요.
examples.en: Unlike soft persimmons, sweet persimmons are sweet even when they're firm.
There is a sweet persimmon tree in my maternal grandmother's yard.
I peeled a sweet persimmon and gave it to the child.

examples.ko: 이 단감이 크고 달아서 선물하기 좋아요.
examples.en: These sweet persimmons are big and sweet, so they're good for gifts.

explain: 떫지 않아서 딱딱한 채로 깎아 먹는 감이에요. 말랑하게 익은 감은 '홍시', 말린 감은 '곶감'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 가을 과일로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I peeled a sweet persimmon and ate it with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딱딱한 단감은 껍질을 깎아서 먹는다는 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing because firm sweet persimmons are peeled before eating.

phrases.en: I got a box of sweet persimmons as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수를 세는 말과 함께 쓰는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A usage with a counting word.

phrases.en: My grandmother likes soft ripe persimmons.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike '단감', this is a soft, fully ripened persimmon.

explain_en: It is a persimmon that is not astringent, so you peel and eat it while still firm. A soft ripe persimmon is '홍시' and a dried one is '곶감', so they are different things. It often comes up as a fall fruit.

examples.en: I rolled out and made the dumpling wrappers myself.
I bought a pack of dumpling wrappers at the supermarket.
The wrapper is so thin that it keeps tearing.
Lightly brush water on the edge of the wrapper.
I made a snack out of the leftover wrappers.

examples.ko: 이 집은 만두피가 쫄깃해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This place is popular because its dumpling skin is chewy.

explain: '만두 껍질'이라고도 말해요. 안에 넣는 '만두소'와 짝으로 외워 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: The dumpling wrapper is thin, so it tears easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만두피'와 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 만두피, widely used in daily speech.

phrases.en: I rolled out dumpling wrappers from flour dough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반죽을 얇게 펴서 만들 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for rolling dough thin to make wrappers.

phrases.en: Wrap the filling in a dumpling wrapper and steam it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만두소를 피로 감싸는 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes wrapping the filling in the wrapper.
phrases.en_equiv: to wrap in a dumpling wrapper

explain_en: People also say '만두 껍질'. It is handy to memorize it as a pair with '만두소', the filling inside.

examples.en: I added a little celery to the salad.

examples.ko: 셀러리는 향이 강해서 안 먹는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Celery has a strong smell, so some people don't eat it.
Please slice the celery stalks thinly.
I bought a bunch of celery at the supermarket.
I drink celery juice every morning.
Celery and onions go into this soup.

explain: 표준 표기는 '셀러리'예요. '샐러리'라고 쓰면 월급을 뜻하는 영어 salary가 떠올라 헷갈릴 수 있으니 조심하세요. 한국 음식에는 자주 안 쓰지만 샐러드나 주스에 많이 넣어요.

phrases.en: I drink celery juice every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 셀러리를 음료로 마실 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when celery is drunk as a beverage.

phrases.example: 셀러리 줄기를 얇게 썰어서 샐러드에 넣었어요.
phrases.en: I sliced the celery stalk thinly and put it in the salad.
phrases.nuance_en: The stalk is the part we mainly eat.

phrases.en: I chop the celery before cooking.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when preparing food.

explain_en: The standard spelling is '셀러리'. Writing '샐러리' can be confused with the English word salary, so be careful. It is not common in traditional Korean cooking, but it is often used in salads and juices.

examples.en: A lot of spices go into Indian cooking.

examples.ko: 저는 향신료 냄새가 강한 음식이 조금 힘들어요.
examples.en: Food with a strong spice smell is a bit hard for me.
I sprinkled spices before grilling the meat.
Pepper and cinnamon are typical spices.

examples.ko: 향신료는 쓰는 양에 따라 맛이 많이 달라져요.
examples.en: With spices, the taste changes a lot depending on how much you use.

examples.ko: 한국 음식은 향신료보다 양념을 많이 써요.
examples.en: Korean food uses more seasoning than spices.

explain: 후추, 계피, 카레 가루처럼 향이 강한 재료를 통틀어 말해요. 한국 음식 이야기에서는 '양념'이라는 말을 더 자주 쓰는데, 양념에는 간장, 고춧가루, 마늘까지 들어가서 범위가 더 넓어요.

phrases.en: I added a little spice to the dish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식에 향이 나는 재료를 더할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for adding aromatic ingredients to food.

phrases.en: This curry has a strong spice smell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식에서 향신료의 향이 세게 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the aroma of spices in food is strong.

phrases.en: Seasoning is important in Korean food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간장, 마늘 같은 것까지 포함해서 범위가 더 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that also includes things like soy sauce and garlic.

explain_en: It covers strongly scented ingredients such as pepper, cinnamon, and curry powder. When talking about Korean food, '양념' is used more often, and it is wider because it includes soy sauce, red pepper powder, and garlic.

examples.en: You peel the shell of pumpkin seeds before eating them.
I roasted pumpkin seeds and ate them as a snack.
I heard pumpkin seeds have many nutrients that are good for the body.
Grandmother dried the pumpkin seeds and set them aside.
I sprinkled pumpkin seeds on top of the salad.

examples.ko: 호박씨 껍질을 까는 데 손이 많이 가요.
examples.en: Peeling pumpkin seeds takes a lot of effort.

explain: 볶아서 간식이나 안주로, 또 샐러드나 죽에 넣어 먹어요. 껍질을 까서 먹는 씨앗이라 '호박씨를 까다'라고 해요. 이 '까다'가 아래 관용 표현에도 쓰여요.

phrases.example: 얌전한 줄 알았는데 뒤에서 호박씨를 깠어요.
phrases.en: I thought he was quiet, but he was up to something behind my back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로는 얌전하고 아무것도 모르는 척하면서 뒤에서 몰래 딴짓을 하거나 제 이익을 챙길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone acts quiet and innocent on the surface but secretly does something else or looks after their own interests behind the scenes.
phrases.en_equiv: do something sneaky behind one's back

explain_en: They are roasted and eaten as a snack, or added to salads and porridge. Since you peel the shell, the verb is '호박씨를 까다'. That same '까다' is used in the idiom below.
